# AlloFlow - WCAG 2.2 Success-Criterion Coverage

<!-- GENERATED by dev-tools/gen_wcag_coverage.cjs - do not edit by hand; re-run after changing the fix registry. -->

This table maps declared repair capabilities in AlloFlow's document-remediation pipeline to WCAG 2.2 criteria. The Automated column is derived from the current SURGICAL_TOOL_REGISTRY in doc_pipeline_source.jsx; a registry tag is an implementation declaration, not validation of an output. Re-run node dev-tools/gen_wcag_coverage.cjs after changing the registry. This map covers document remediation only; the [current ACR](../VPAT-2.5-WCAG-AlloFlow.md) covers the application's separate scope and evidence gaps.

## Honest summary

The active WCAG 2.2 A/AA catalog has **55** criteria. This map classifies **20** as routinely relevant to static document content:

- **11** have a dedicated automated repair capability. Active A/AA rows reference **32** registry tools across **11** criteria; AAA and obsolete tags are excluded from these counts.
- **6** have construction support, such as struct-tree or semantic-HTML mechanisms. Actual reading order, reflow and other output behavior still require verification.
- **3** require human judgment and lack a reliable automated repair.
- **30** are conditional on relevant forms, media or interactive HTML.

The remaining **5** are classified N/A only for the assumed noninteractive static-document scope. Conditional rows are listed Conditional, not N/A. Inspect each actual document and embedded content to establish applicability; this classification does not justify exclusions from the whole-product ACR.

> **This is a self-reported capability map, not a conformance claim.** Automated means a tool attempts a repair; Structural means an implementation mechanism exists. Neither proves that a criterion is satisfied. Record validation against actual output bytes. PDF structure checks such as veraPDF, web automation and AI review have distinct limits; meaningful alternatives, reading order and complete WCAG outcomes still require human review. Regeneration of this map is not a new document or assistive-technology evaluation.
